title: Same-Month Return Customer Rate
description: For each calendar month, report the **returning customer rate**: the fraction of that month's distinct buyers who had also made a purchase in the **previous** calendar month. Name the columns `month`, `returning_customers`, `total` and `rate`, where `rate` = `returning_customers / total` rounded to 2 decimals. Return months in chronological order. A month's `total` is its distinct buyers (a customer counts once even with several purchases).
solutionSql:
WITH purchases AS (
  SELECT customer_id, strftime('%Y-%m', order_date) AS month
  FROM orders
  GROUP BY customer_id, strftime('%Y-%m', order_date)
)
SELECT cur.month,
       COUNT(DISTINCT prev.customer_id) AS returning_customers,
       COUNT(DISTINCT cur.customer_id) AS total,
       ROUND(COUNT(DISTINCT prev.customer_id) * 1.0 / COUNT(DISTINCT cur.customer_id), 2) AS rate
FROM purchases cur
LEFT JOIN purchases prev
  ON prev.customer_id = cur.customer_id
 AND prev.month = strftime('%Y-%m', cur.month || '-01', '-1 month')
GROUP BY cur.month
ORDER BY cur.month;
hint: A buyer is 'returning' that month only if they also appear in the prior month. Self-join the per-customer, per-month set, shifting one month back with strftime.
outputExplanation: February: 2 distinct buyers (10, 30), of which only customer 10 bought in January too, so rate = 1/2 = 0.5.
